messages:
leah: Quick sync — StratusMed POC run this morning showed unexpected jitter during a sustained ramp. Need help on two fronts: (1) tweak the load plan so we can reproduce reliably, and (2) figure out burst pricing + HSM/KMS implications for their security needs. Posting raw numbers below.

sam: Can you paste the test command and the p95/p99 numbers? Also what's their acceptance criteria?

leah: Acceptance: p99 inference latency < 250ms, steady-state p50 ~120ms. Test was a k6-based driver hitting our /v1/generate hosted endpoint (us-west-2). Quick snippet we ran:

```bash
k6 run --vus 200 --duration 15m script.js 
# script ramps to 450 QPS in waves; each request sends a 512-token prompt
```

Observed (aggregated over 15m):
- avg: 140ms
- p95: 320ms
- p99: 1,200ms (spikes correlated with bursts)
- error rate: 0.2% (mostly 5xx from gateway timeout)

Repro: spikes show up every 2-3 minutes for ~10-20s during ramp phases.

diego: Thanks. A few immediate questions: were you testing against Hosted or Dedicated capacity? Which model + quant profile?

leah: Hosted (default tenant), model: redwood-3b-instruct, quantized medium. We didn't enable KV prefix caching or batching in the client.

diego: Ok — that explains a lot. Quick theory: when we see periodic spikes during bursts it's usually queue pile-up + cold worker spin-up or backpressure from external KMS/HSM calls if signing keys are fetched per request. Two suggested mitigations to validate:
1) Rerun against a small Dedicated pool (2 GPUs) so you avoid noisy‑neighbor spin-ups.
2) Enable KV cache + continuous batching in the client (batch size cap ~32, max latency 20ms) so the runtime can smooth token throughput.

sam: Can you share an example curl showing how the client is currently calling the API?

leah: Current simple test call:

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate" -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"redwood-3b-instruct","prompt":"<512-token-prompt>","max_tokens":64}'
```

diego: For the next run, switch to the streaming endpoint and enable the SDK's batching flag. If you can't switch, at least pin the run to Dedicated: that should remove worker allocation noise.

aaron: Pricing note for the sales thread: we can grant a short Dedicated burst addon for POCs — billable by the minute/hour depending on region. Example conservative estimate for DOE: 2x A10 GPUs for 4 hours = ~ $XX/hr per GPU * 4 hours -> I'll compute exacts with finance, but expect a few hundred dollars for the short trial. For sustained Dedicated (monthly commit) we offer discounts. Also, if they require HSM-backed keys in Private deployment, there's an initial setup fee + higher TCO for private control plane. I'll put numbers in a follow-up.

leah: Important: StratusMed's security team insists on HSM-backed signing for PHI ingestion. They flagged a potential blocker: any KMS roundtrip per request might add latency they consider unacceptable. Thoughts on HSM latency impact?

diego: Good point. HSM/KMS overhead depends on integration pattern:
- If each request performs an on-line KMS encrypt/decrypt call, expect 15–60ms extra per operation (network + HSM op).
- Best practice: envelope encryption with locally cached DEKs (data encryption keys) and use the HSM for key wrapping/unwrapping only on rotation. That approach adds ~2–5ms per request for local ops plus occasional 50–100ms for rotation events.

So for their p99 target, we strongly recommend caching DEKs client-side and avoiding per-request KMS calls during inference. If they still need per-request HSM ops for compliance, we should plan for Dedicated or Private and factor ~100–150ms headroom into p99.

sam: Can ops-bot run a short experiment: simulate per-request KMS latency (50ms) injected and show the effect on p99?

ops-bot: Scheduled synthetic run: 200 VUs, 12m duration, injected 50ms KMS latency in the call path. Run id: run-350999-a1. Results will post to #eng-runtime when complete. :gear:

leah: Great. Other enterprise blockers from the prospect side: VPN/IP allowlist, SCIM for SSO, SOC2 attestation copy request. Also they asked whether Private deployment supports HSM integration with Azure Key Vault / AWS CloudHSM.

aaron: Private supports both Azure Key Vault and CloudHSM; we expose a KMIP-compatible proxy for on-prem HSMs. For the questionnaire: provide the SOC2 report, details on key custody with HSMs, and a short writeup on our recommended envelope pattern. I'll draft the security blurb.

diego: Next technical steps for validation:
- Run the same k6 script pinned to a 2-GPU Dedicated pool with batching + KV cache enabled.
- Run a synthetic with 50ms KMS injection to quantify p99 delta.
- If p99 still >250ms, try increasing GPUs or reducing tokenization cost (shorter prompts, 256 tokens).

leah: Timeline: customer asks for an updated run + cost estimate by EOD Wednesday. Can we meet that?

aaron: I can compute burst pricing today and send a ballpark by EOD. If we need finance-level numbers, give me 24h.

diego: I can kick off the Dedicated run this afternoon once Ops grants a temp pool. @ops-bot, please spin up pool-3509 (2x A10 equiv) for 6h.

ops-bot: pool-3509 scheduled. ETA 18 minutes.

leah: Thanks all. Once we have run results, I'll update StratusMed and ask them to sign the narrow scope NDA for Private demo (they're happy to do that). Can someone own the security questionnaire updates?

aaron: I'll own the security writeup + HSM integration section.

sam: I'll own the updated test script with batching flags and a short checklist of config changes we recommend for the prospect.

diego: I'll run the Dedicated soak and post the raw logs + p95/p99 breakdown.

leah: Perfect. Marking action items: 1) Dedicated soak (diego), 2) KMS latency sim (ops-bot/diego), 3) burst pricing ballpark (aaron), 4) security questionnaire + SOC2 + HSM writeup (aaron).

leah: If we get p99 under 300ms with HSM-envelope pattern, sales can proceed to contract stage. Otherwise we need to scope Private deployment timeline.

aaron: noted. I'll include the Private deployment setup time estimate in the follow-up.

diego: quick tip for the run: set k6 thresholds to fail early if p99 > 600ms so we don't waste time. Also capture JVM/GPU metrics with the runtime probe.

leah: Thanks — will do. :thumbsup:
